# Contributor Code of Conduct

## Our pledge

We want SoundControl to be a place where someone can debug a Bluetooth protocol
at 2 a.m. without being made to feel stupid. As contributors and maintainers we
pledge to make participation a harassment-free experience for everyone,
regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex
characteristics, gender identity and expression, experience level, education,
socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or
sexual identity and orientation.

## Standards

**Do**

- Assume good faith: a "the app is broken" report usually means "my device
  behaves differently than you assumed".
- Say what you tested and what you could not test — hardware projects live and
  die by that honesty.
- Give the reason, not just the verdict: "this opcode needs a captured frame
  first" teaches; "no" does not.
- Keep the project's constraints visible: no accounts, no telemetry, no bloat.

**Don't**

- Gatekeep device ownership, or dismiss someone for using a phone app.
- Publish exploit payloads, capture-only firmware images, or another person's
  MAC addresses and device names in an issue.
- Take potshots at Anker's engineers, or argue that reverse-engineering for
  interoperability is itself misconduct — this project documents a protocol so
  that earbuds keep working without an account.

## Enforcement

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behaviour may be
reported to the project maintainer through a
[private security advisory](https://github.com/Shankers8811/soundcontrol/security/advisories/new)
or by e-mail to the account that owns this repository. Reports are reviewed and
investigated promptly and fairly, and the reporter's identity is kept private.

Contributors asked to stop behaviour that violates this policy must do so
immediately. Repeated violations, publishing unpatched exploit details, or
harassment of another contributor can lead to removal from the project.
